# munitoai-free rate_limit_rpm: 15 — 24h observation check-in

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want a 24-hour post-change verification that the new
`rate_limit_rpm: 15` on `munitoai-free` (raised from 10 by
LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4) does **not** drive the third-party free tier into
sustained upstream 429s, and that the predicted paid-spill reduction actually
materialises — with an explicit rollback trigger if it does not.

## Context

- LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 measured the pre-change state: at `rate_limit_rpm: 10`
  the free-tier spill was ~45 % of arrivals at peak demand (2.5 h window,
  p95 32 arrivals/min), paid (opencode.ai) share ~46 % of remote dispatches,
  upstream 429s 2 in 2.5 h (0.17 % of free dispatches). The pre-gate 429 onset
  was ≈20 dispatches/rolling-60 s (429-minute rate: 4–6 % at ≤19/min, 20 % at
  20–29, 47 % at 30–39, 100 % ≥40). The what-if simulation at capacity 15
  predicted spill ≈27 %.
- The value was changed to 15 in `proxy/config.yaml` and `proxy/config-fast.yaml`
  (all three chains: plan / author / code) with `provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio: 0.3`
  unchanged → new-session effective cap now **11**, affinity cap **15**.
- The change takes effect at the **next proxy restart** (T0). It was NOT
  restarted as part of LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4; the observation window starts at
  whichever restart first carries the new config. If the restart has not
  happened, this check-in must wait and re-schedule rather than measure the old
  config.
- Reproducible measurement tool: `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`
  (committed with LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4).

## Evaluation method (24 h observation window [T0, T0+24h])

1. **Restart marker:** find the first `Proxy restart attribution:` (or
   `Logging initialised at`) line in `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` after the
   LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 commit/push; that is T0. If none exists, wait (the change
   is not live).
2. **Upstream 429s:** count
   `upstream error status=429 url=https://api.munito.ai` lines in [T0, T0+24h).
   Report absolute count, per hour, and as a share of munitoai dispatches
   (`[remote] POST … -> https://api.munito.ai/inference`).
3. **Rollback trigger:** if the upstream-429 *minute* rate at peak demand
   (≥ 20 free arrivals in a rolling-60 s) exceeds ~10 % of minutes, or any
   sustained multi-minute 429 burst occurs, **revert to 10** (config + fixtures +
   tests + docs, mirroring the change in LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4) and record why.
4. **Spill confirmation:** run
   `python3 proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py` over the window and report
   the measured spill share at capacity 15 (expected ≈27 %, vs 45 % at 10) and
   the paid (opencode.ai) share of remote dispatches.
5. **Latency:** confirm waits stay ≤ 15 s (0 waits > 15 s) and MunitoAI
   first-token p90/p95/p99 does not rise vs the pre-change baseline.
6. Post the measurement table on this item (AC1-equivalent) and, when all
   rollback conditions are clear, mark it `in_review`/`completed`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The measured upstream-429 rate over [T0, T0+24h) is reported (absolute,
   per-hour, share of dispatches) with an explicit pass/fail against the
   rollback trigger.
2. The measured spill share and paid-tier share are reported and compared to
   the LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4 predictions (≈27 % spill at 15).
3. Latency (wait distribution ≤ 15 s; free-tier first-token p50/p90/p95/p99) is
   reported and compared to baseline.
4. An explicit verdict is recorded: keep 15 / revert to 10 / adjust further,
   with the evidence, and the item advanced to `in_review`.
5. If the verdict is revert/adjust, the config, fixtures, tests and docs are
   updated in a worktree and the full project test suite passes (via the test
   skill).

## Constraints

- Do not restart the proxy from this session; if the config is not yet live,
  wait and re-schedule rather than measuring stale state.
- Test runs go through the test skill; never drive the free tier into sustained
  429s to probe.
- Read-only on production state except the revert path (AC5), which is its own
  approved change.

data.description:
## Problem statement

The proxy's `low` priority route (used by the priority-window cheap slot, 01:00–10:00 local, plus any explicit `X-Priority: low`) currently chains as `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` for the plan/author/code models. When the 2 local slots are saturated (a common overnight condition — see the 2026-10-19 proxy-usage-analysis report: fallback_after_queue 1657, munitoai-free rate limiting), low-priority traffic falls straight through to `munitoai-free`, which is capped at `rate_limit_rpm: 15` and returns HTTP 429s (16 upstream 429 events in the last window). Meanwhile the opencode-go provider entries sit idle and available during their off-peak UTC windows (`["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`, added by LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P) — precisely the hours when the cheap priority window is active and local is most contended.

Goal: allow low-priority work items to fall back to opencode-go when opencode-go is inside its off-peak `available_times` windows, so overflow local work during cheap hours is absorbed by an idle paid tier instead of being dropped on the rate-limited free tier.

## Context / constraints

- `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code is `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` (`proxy/config.yaml`). The `compact` model's low chain is `[opencode-go-compact, deepseek-flash-compact]` and is NOT in scope unless explicitly decided.
- The "low never spends on paid remote tiers" invariant (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA AC2 / priority.py `priority_routing_profile`) must be relaxed **only for off-peak-window-gated opencode-go entries** — the `available_times` gate (`provider.py _is_within_allowed_window`) keeps the paid spend confined to off-peak hours. Spending must remain blocked outside those windows.
- opencode-go entries in the plan/author/code model chains: `opencode-go` (OPENCODE_API_KEY), `opencode-go-2` (OPENCODE_2_API_KEY), `opencode-go-3` (OPENCODE_3_API_KEY) — all carry `available_times: ["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`.
- `available_times` are expressed in UTC; the cheap priority window is local time. Decide the intended alignment explicitly (and document it), since local vs UTC interpretation determines which hours opencode-go is actually reachable.

## Scope

Config + routing logic only. No llama-server changes. Evidence collection uses the proxy-usage-analysis skill (CLI: `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`) before and after.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Low-chain entry added:** the `low` priority_routes for plan, author and code include at least one opencode-go entry (after `munitoai-free`), with spend confined to the entry's off-peak `available_times` windows.
2. **Off-peak gating verified:** a unit test proves that when the opencode-go entry is outside its `available_times` window the low chain skips it (falls through to the next eligible provider), and inside the window it is tried — mirroring the existing timing-gate behaviour for other providers.
3. **Low-chain order preserved:** `local-qwen3` remains first when local has capacity; `munitoai-free` is attempted before paid opencode-go (free tier always preferred over paid when both are viable).
4. **Priority semantics intact:** medium/high chains are unchanged; the fully-paid `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` entries are NOT added to the low chain.
5. **No regression in retry-after / cooldown bookkeeping:** an off-peak opencode-go 5xx/429 does not poison the provider cooldown or stall circuit breaker for medium/high traffic (existing per-provider failure counters shared, not reset).
6. **Doc updated:** `proxy/config.yaml` `priority_routes.low` comments (and priority.py docstring if it states the paid-tier invariant) describe the off-peak opencode-go exception, including the UTC vs local window alignment decision.
7. **Tests + report:** full suite passes via `/skill:test`; run the proxy-usage-analysis report for a full window after the change and comment the work item with the before/after fallback-reason delta (`large_context_bypass`/`fallback_after_queue`/`context_too_large`/HTTP 429 counts), demonstrating that a share of low-priority overflow now lands on opencode-go during off-peak hours without increasing overall paid spend outside those windows.
data.title: Enable low-priority fallback to opencode-go during its off-peak windows

## Goal

Add unit-test coverage for the off-peak-windowed low-priority fallback **before** the config/logic change, so the behaviour is pinned by tests (test-first).

## Scope

Tests only. No production behaviour change in this item.

## Work

1. Test that a `low`-priority chain entry carrying `available_times` is **skipped** when the current UTC time is outside the window (`provider.py::_is_within_allowed_window` → `Skipping provider=...: outside its available_times window (UTC)`), and the resolver falls through to the next eligible provider.
2. Test that the same entry is **selected** when inside the window.
3. Test that a window-gated entry appended after a non-gated free-tier entry does not change resolution when the free tier is available (behaviour-neutral outside the window).
4. Test `priority_routes.low` chain order for plan/author/code resolves to `local-qwen3 → munitoai-free → <opencode-go entry>` (this test will fail until the config item lands — that is the intended TDD red state; mark it `xfail`/skip only if the repo convention requires green main between items, and document the choice).
5. Test that `medium`/`high` chains are unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Tests exist covering in-window selection, out-of-window skip-and-fall-through, and behaviour-neutrality when the free tier is available.
2. A test asserts the intended `low` chain order for plan, author and code.
3. A test asserts `medium`/`high` chains are unchanged.
4. Tests follow existing proxy test conventions (fixtures, `available_times` timing monkeypatching — reuse the pattern used by the existing timing-gate tests rather than inventing a new one).
5. `pytest proxy/tests/` passes (or is in a documented, intentional red state for the not-yet-landed config assertion).
data.title: Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating

data.description:
## Goal

Allow `low`-priority requests to fall back to an opencode-go entry when that entry is inside its off-peak `available_times` window, so local-slot overflow during cheap hours is absorbed instead of hitting the rate-limited free tier.

## Background (measured)

- `low` chain today (plan/author/code): `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]`.
- `munitoai-free` is budget-gated at `rate_limit_rpm: 15`; over-budget requests from **new** sessions pass straight through to the next tier (`LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`), so a further entry catches exactly the 429/rate-limit overflow.
- Window-gated entries are skipped with `continue` (`provider.py` around line 2079), so appending opencode-go after `munitoai-free` is behaviour-neutral when the window is closed.
- **UTC/local alignment:** `available_times` are **UTC**; the priority cheap window (01:00–10:00) is **local `Europe/Dublin` = UTC 00:00–09:00** in summer time. opencode-go is unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00, so only **~3 of the 9 cheap hours** (UTC 00:00–01:00 and 04:00–06:00) gain the new tier. This is expected and is the point of "off-peak only" — no paid spend occurs in the gap windows.

## Work

1. Append an opencode-go entry to `priority_routes.low` for the `plan`, `author` and `code` models in `proxy/config.yaml`, ordered **after** `munitoai-free`.
2. Choose which entry (`opencode-go`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go-3`) and record the rationale; prefer the same key the medium/high chain uses first, falling back to the next key if that chain's ordering argues otherwise.
3. Update the `priority_routes` explanatory comment (and the `priority.py::priority_routing_profile` docstring if it states the "low never spends on paid tiers" invariant) to describe the off-peak exception and the UTC-vs-local overlap.
4. Leave `medium`/`high` chains, `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` untouched — no fully-paid entry joins the low chain.
5. Leave the `compact` model's low chain (`opencode-go-compact → deepseek-flash-compact`) untouched unless a follow-up item says otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `priority_routes.low` for plan, author and code is `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free, <opencode-go entry>]` in `proxy/config.yaml`.
2. The chosen opencode-go entry carries `available_times: ["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]` (unchanged).
3. `medium` and `high` chains are byte-identical to before this change; `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` do not appear in any `low` chain.
4. Outside the window the resolution order is identical to today (test from the test item proves this).
5. `proxy/config.yaml` parses via `yaml.safe_load` and the proxy test suite passes via `/skill:test`.
6. Comments/docstring document the off-peak exception and state the UTC-vs-local overlap (~3 of 9 cheap hours), so the next reader does not mistake it for full cheap-window coverage.

data.description:
## Goal

Prove the change does what it claims on real traffic: low-priority overflow lands on opencode-go during its off-peak windows, and paid spend does not increase outside those windows.

## Work

1. Capture the **baseline** from the pre-change window using the proxy-usage-analysis skill CLI:
   `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`
   Record: `rate_limited`, `fallback_after_queue`, `empty_response`, `HTTP 429`/`HTTP 503` counts, per-model token share, and the `munitoai-free` share.
2. After the change has run for one full 24 h window, re-run the same CLI and diff the same metrics.
3. Confirm in `proxy.log` that `Fallback triggered ... to=<opencode-go entry>` events occur for low-priority traffic **only** inside the `available_times` windows, and that no such event occurs in the UTC 01:00–04:00 / 06:00–10:00 gaps.
4. Comment the parent work item with the before/after table and a short verdict.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A before/after metrics table is recorded on the parent work item (LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX).
2. Log evidence shows at least one low-priority fallback to the opencode-go entry inside an off-peak window, OR a documented explanation of why none occurred (e.g. local capacity never overflowed in the window).
3. Log evidence shows **zero** low-priority fallbacks to the opencode-go entry inside the UTC gap windows (01:00–04:00, 06:00–10:00).
4. The report shows whether `rate_limited` / HTTP 429 volume from `api.munito.ai` fell in the overlap hours, with an honest statement if the change was too small to move the number.
5. A clear cost statement: did total paid-tier token share increase outside the overlap hours? If yes, treat as a regression and record it.

## Appendix: planning questions & decisions

Recorded by the `plan` skill session `herdr-1792390902-3844878-15177`.

### Q1. Which opencode-go entry joins the low chain?
`proxy/config.yaml` defines three equivalent entries: `opencode-go-3` (OPENCODE_3_API_KEY), `opencode-go-2` (OPENCODE_2_API_KEY), `opencode-go` (OPENCODE_API_KEY), all with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and identical `available_times`.
**Answer (eng, recommended, for confirmation):** `opencode-go-3` — it is first in the medium/high provider lists for the code model, so reusing it for the low chain keeps prompt-cache affinity aligned with the hot path. Evidence: `proxy/config.yaml` model `code` → `providers[2].name == opencode-go-3`.
**Status:** OPEN QUESTION (confirm at implementation).

### Q2. UTC vs local window alignment
`available_times` are **UTC**; the priority cheap window (`priority_window: 01:00–10:00`) is **local time**.
**Research:** host timezone is `Europe/Dublin` (IST, +0100 in October), so the cheap window is UTC **00:00–09:00**. opencode-go windows are UTC `["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`, i.e. unavailable UTC `01:00–04:00` and `06:00–10:00`. Overlap = UTC `00:00–01:00` + `04:00–06:00` = **3 of 9 cheap hours**. Evidence: `date -u` output and `proxy/config.yaml` `available_times` / `priority_window`.
**Answer (recommended):** keep `available_times` unchanged — "off-peak only" is the requirement, and the gaps are deliberate paid-spend avoidance. Document the 3-of-9 overlap in config comments so the limitation is explicit rather than surprising.
**Status:** decided for this item; the widening question is an OPEN QUESTION below.

### OPEN QUESTION (operator): widen the windows?
The change yields ~3 extra hours of local-overflow capacity per night, not 9. If more cheap-window coverage is wanted, opencode-go `available_times` would need to cover UTC `01:00–04:00` and `06:00–10:00` too — which means paid spend in the currently-excluded hours. This item deliberately does **not** do that. Directed to the operator; matters because it is the difference between a 3-hour and a 9-hour fix.

### Q3. Should the `compact` model's low chain change?
`compact` already chains `low: [opencode-go-compact, deepseek-flash-compact]` — it has no local tier and already leads with opencode-go.
**Answer (eng):** no. Out of scope; leave untouched.

### Duplicate-work check
`wl search "opencode-go"` / `"off-peak"` / `"low priority"` reviewed. Nearest neighbours: LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P (added the off-peak `available_times` windows — prerequisite, completed), LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA (introduced priority routing and the `low = local + free` chain — the constraint being relaxed here, completed), LP-0MSMIPPJI007GU9N (cheap mode keeps remote enabled — completed). **No duplicate found:** none adds opencode-go to a `low` chain.

## Plan decomposition (3 features, test-first)

| # | Feature | Item | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating | LP-0MVF1FM9500070U1 | — |
| 2 | Add opencode-go to low-priority routes (off-peak) | LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I | #1 |
| 3 | Verify off-peak low-priority fallback in a live window | LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO | #2 |

Test-first ordering: the gating/ordering tests (item 1) land before the config change (item 2); live verification (item 3) follows the change.

**Vertical slice per phase:** each item delivers code/config + tests + docs + observability end-to-end (item 2 owns the config *and* its doc comments; item 3 owns the measurement against the proxy-usage-analysis report).

**Key files:** `proxy/config.yaml` (priority_routes, model chains, comments noted), `proxy/proxy/priority.py` (`priority_routing_profile` docstring), `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_is_within_allowed_window` — read-only, behaviour reused), `proxy/tests/` (new gating/ordering tests).

**Effort:** S (config + tests + docs; no new routing mechanism). **Risk:** Low (window gate makes it behaviour-neutral outside off-peak; append-only chain change; fully reversible by removing one list entry).

**Scope decision:** planning was performed rather than auto-complete because the UTC-vs-local window overlap (Q2) materially changes the expected benefit (3 of 9 hours) and needed to be evidenced before implementation, and because a test-first item was required to pin the fall-through behaviour.
